questions.question: In the model, what is the role of κ(x₂ − x₁) in the first oscillator's x equation?

answers.b: It couples oscillator 1 to oscillator 2 through their x values.
answers.c: It changes the parameter a in the y equation.
answers.d: It adds random noise to oscillator 1.

explanations.a: Time is represented by t; this term describes coupling.
explanations.b: Correct. The term depends on the x difference and is scaled by the coupling strength κ.
explanations.c: The parameter a is fixed in the y equation.
explanations.d: The model is deterministic and this term is not random noise.

questions.question: What does a small, sustained RMS error indicate in this experiment?

answers.a: The recent x₁ and x₂ signals are close on average.
answers.c: The phase portrait is a time series.

explanations.a: Correct. RMS error summarizes the recent magnitude of the x-signal difference.
explanations.b: Small difference does not mean the signals are stationary.
explanations.c: The phase portrait plots state variables against one another.
explanations.d: At zero coupling the systems evolve independently; the error is not forced to be small.

questions.question: Why should you observe the error over time instead of relying on one low reading?

answers.a: A brief dip may not represent sustained agreement between the signals.
answers.b: The error plot only works once.
answers.c: The RMS error is the same as the coupling slider value.
answers.d: A single reading changes the equations.

explanations.a: Correct. Sustained low error and overlapping traces provide stronger evidence than a brief dip.
explanations.b: The error plot updates continuously as the model runs.
explanations.c: RMS error is calculated from the signal difference, not copied from κ.
explanations.d: A displayed reading does not alter the equations.

questions.question: What is a phase portrait in this simulation?

answers.a: A graph of x against elapsed simulation time
answers.b: A graph of x against y for each oscillator
answers.c: A chart of the quiz score against κ
answers.d: A table of the fixed parameters only

explanations.b: Correct. Each path shows the relationship between x and y as the system evolves.
explanations.c: The simulator does not graph quiz scores.
explanations.d: The phase portrait uses evolving state variables.

questions.question: Which conclusion is best supported by the simulator?

answers.a: Every pair of chaotic oscillators synchronizes for any nonzero coupling.
answers.b: The model proves all real oscillators behave exactly like the simulation.
answers.c: For the selected model and settings, coupling can reduce the difference; the plots should be checked for sustained agreement.
answers.d: Synchronization can be identified from the coupling value alone.

explanations.a: Synchronization depends on the model and parameter values; it is not guaranteed for every nonzero coupling.
explanations.b: This is an idealized numerical model and does not represent every physical system.
explanations.c: Correct. The conclusion is limited to the model and should be supported by the observed signals and error.
explanations.d: The state trajectories and their error provide the relevant evidence.
